title: Chu Berry's pipe and watch
summary: Hinton produces the pipe and watch he picked up at the crash scene and recalls Chu's delirious words about his change.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: While you're talking about this, look at this.
Oh, that was his pipe.
This is the pipe he had in his mouth and this was his watch.
That's right, that's right, that he had.
I picked this up when I stepped out of the bus.
See, that's the pipe he had in the automobile accident, and he picked it up. There it is.
And the watch. His watch fell out of the band.
Uh-huh. Oh, wow.
That wasn't yesterday.
I know.
You're right. I remember it so very well because he got finished --
That was November 1941.
1941. Brother, you're amazing for dates.
That's right. It was November 1941. That's right.
That's amazing.

That's right.

Uh-huh. I know.

-- just as you say (unintelligible). And I looked around for money and all I could see was some pennies on the road and then I saw his pipe, which is here sitting before us -- it was broken into three pieces -- and he still had the band on his wrist.
Uh-huh.

hit the side of the road and it knocked the watch out of the band because the watch was -- the band was still on his wrist.
